scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service canceled 34 days ago, which is slightly outside the standard 30-day refund window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Claire Sullivan and I'm 43. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?

Hello Claire, thank you for reaching out. I understand how frustrating it can be to return from travel and find unexpected charges. I would be happy to look into this for you. To get started, could you please provide the email address associated with your account and the transaction ID for the charge in question?
Sure, the email is claire.sullivan@email.com and the transaction ID is TXN-99284-ABC.
Thank you, Claire. I have located your account. For security, could you please confirm the last four digits of the payment method used for this transaction?

Thank you for verifying those details. I see the cancellation was processed 34 days ago. While our 'Service Terms and Refund Policy' strictly limits automatic refunds to within 30 days of the billing date, I can see you have been a loyal customer for over three years. Given the circumstances, I am authorized to make a one-time exception for you.
Oh, that would be wonderful. Thank you so much for understanding!

You're very welcome. I have successfully processed the refund of $49.99 back to your card ending in 4492. You should see the credit reflect in your account within 3-5 business days depending on your bank. Is there anything else I can assist you with today?

resolution_summary: The agent verified the customer's identity and transaction, acknowledged the policy limit, but utilized discretionary authority to grant a one-time exception for the refund due to customer loyalty.

judge_scores.justification: The agent executed appropriate security verification, communicated with genuine warmth and specific acknowledgment of the customer's travel situation, and efficiently gathered all necessary information without redundant turns. Furthermore, the agent correctly cited the 30-day refund policy while successfully exercising authorized discretionary judgment to resolve the request without unnecessary escalation.
